intro: VulnBench 2.0 takes the next steps JS 1.0 named: application-scale fixtures, an independent ground truth and stricter scoring. Its numbers are not comparable with JS 1.0's.

rows.js10: Can LLMs find the same bugs twice? Repeatability and agreement.
rows.v20: What do AI security agents find that SAST does not, and what do they miss?

rows.js10: Ten small JavaScript and Express projects
rows.v20: 20 open-source web applications in Go, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python and Java

rows.js10: Snyk Code's findings define the reference set
rows.v20: Curated, attacker-reachable vulnerabilities with annotated source-to-sink flows and author-verified exploits; not derived from any tool's findings

rows.js10: Same vulnerability type; file and line not required
rows.v20: Class plus source and sink, each within two lines; one finding credited to at most one vulnerability

rows.js10: Claude configurations through one agentic harness, plus Snyk Code reproducing its own reference
rows.v20: Productized harnesses: Snyk Code, Claude Code /security-review, Codex Security, DeepSec

rows.js10: Five identical runs per configuration and project
rows.v20: One run per configuration and application; Snyk Code repeated twice more in supplementary runs
Attacker-Reachable Vulnerability Recall (macro, with the matched count); DeepSec scored with localized recall

boundary: Snyk Code's 100% in JS 1.0 is reproduction of the reference set it defined; in 2.0 Snyk Code is scored against an independent reference set like every other configuration. Never compare a 2.0 number with a JS 1.0 number.
